Two focused improvements to the Nxeon platform (Next.js + Prisma + Postgres). Work ONLY in the ISOLATED worktree /opt/nxeon-build-polish (branch feature/nxeon-polish, off main 618626f).

=== ABSOLUTE ISOLATION (a prior run broke prod by ignoring this) ===
- Do ALL work in /opt/nxeon-build-polish. NEVER touch /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging (no cd/build/writes/git there).
- First: `cd /opt/nxeon-build-polish && npm ci` for this worktree's OWN node_modules. Run prisma generate / build / tests ONLY here. Verify pwd + branch before building.
- NEVER systemctl/restart/deploy, never `prisma db push` any DB, never edit .env.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` MUST be 0 errors. (Note: a full `next build` can't finish here because the isolated worktree has no DATABASE_URL for static-prerender of pre-existing DB pages — that's expected/environmental; rely on tsc + tests + webpack-compile. Do NOT try to point at prod's DB.)

=== TASK 1 — Multi-brand Studio ===
The Marketing Hub "Studio" (lib/marketing/templates.ts + app/admin/marketing/studio + components/admin/marketing/StudioClient.tsx + MarketingAsset model) currently renders creatives only in the Nxeon brand. Add BRAND support so it can also produce Sitewave and Adloop creatives:
- Add a Brand palette registry (pure): Nxeon (navy #0B1224, panels #141E3A/#182647, violet #7C5CFF, cyan #22D3EE, ink #EAF0FF, violet→cyan gradient); Sitewave (indigo #4F46E5, coral #FB7185, ink #0B1020, cloud #F8FAFC); Adloop (emerald #10B981, amber #F59E0B, slate-900 #0F172A, mist #CBD5E1). Each with a name + wordmark + tagline default (Sitewave "Websites that win you customers.", Adloop "Your ads, on autopilot.").
- renderTemplate(templateKey, values) gains a `brand` param that swaps palette + wordmark. Keep all templates working for every brand.
- Studio UI: a brand selector; the live preview + saved asset reflect the chosen brand. Store the brand on MarketingAsset (additive field `brand String @default("nxeon")`). Keep client-side PNG rasterization.
- Add/extend tests for the palette registry + brand-aware render (e.g. each brand's key colors appear in output; unknown brand falls back to nxeon).

=== TASK 2 — Fix the pre-existing failing tests ===
Run `npm test` (or `npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts`) and identify the ~6-7 FAILING tests that pre-exist on main (reports named: a login-form state test, a signup retention test, an unguarded export in lib/actions-contact.ts, a leftmost-XFF/IP test, a webmail/MX host test, and a mailcow ordering test, an smtp_pass test). For each: investigate the root cause and FIX it properly — where the test is brittle, fix the test; where it reveals a genuine small bug (e.g. an unguarded server action export that SHOULD check auth — that's a real security fix worth doing), fix the code correctly and safely. 
IMPORTANT: If any failure reveals a change that is risky to make blind (touches money, auth in a non-obvious way, or live behavior you can't fully verify), do NOT force it — leave that test as-is and clearly REPORT it with your analysis instead. Goal: get the suite green where it's safe, and surface anything that isn't.

When done (in /opt/nxeon-build-polish): tsc 0 errors; run the full test suite and report the before/after failing count; commit + `git push` feature/nxeon-polish. Report: what multi-brand changes you made, each failing test and how you resolved it (fixed test / fixed bug / left + why), and the final test tally. Do NOT deploy, do NOT touch prod.

The `clientIp` function takes anything with a `.get()` method (like the result of `await headers()`) and returns a validated IP string, defaulting to `UNKNOWN_IP` if nothing's found—it never returns null.
